steps: Learn the key vocabulary for film types and TV programmes
Master the preterite of ver (vi, viste, vio) and ser/ir (fue) for past viewing
Practise opinion phrases beyond me gusta: me encanta, no soporto, prefiero
Build extended sentences using porque and comparatives
method_card.title: TV, Film and Streaming
method_card.content:
This lesson covers vocabulary for TV programmes, film genres and streaming habits, plus opinion phrases and the preterite tense for talking about what you watched.

SpanishEnglish
la películafilm
la serieTV series
el programaprogramme
el canalchannel
el documentaldocumentary
los dibujos animadoscartoons / animated film
el telediario / las noticiasnews
ver en streamingto stream / watch via streaming
una película de acciónaction film
una película de terrorhorror film
una comediacomedy
emocionanteexciting
entretenido/aentertaining
conmovedor/amoving, touching
me encanta(n)I love (it / them)

Grammar focus — preterite of ver and ser: To talk about past viewing, use the preterite. Ver is irregular: vi (I watched), vio (he/she watched). Ser shares preterite forms with ir: fue (it was). Use the imperfect era to describe a background feeling. Examples: Vi una película de acción anoche — fue muy emocionante. (I watched an action film last night — it was very exciting.)

Model paragraph: Mi programa favorito es una serie que veo en streaming. El fin de semana pasado vi una comedia con mi familia y fue muy divertida. No me gustan los documentales porque los encuentro aburridos. (My favourite programme is a series I watch via streaming. Last weekend I watched a comedy with my family and it was very funny. I don't like documentaries because I find them boring.)

exam_context.frequency: Core topic — TV, film and streaming appear across all papers

steps: Learn the key vocabulary for music genres, instruments and concerts
Master desde hace + present tense for ongoing duration (not the perfect tense)
Build extended sentences combining opinions and comparatives with connectives
method_card.title: Music and Listening Habits
method_card.content:
This lesson covers music genres, listening habits, instruments and concerts, plus two key grammar structures: comparatives and desde hace + present for ongoing duration.

SpanishEnglish
la músicamusic
la canciónsong
el cantante / la cantantesinger (m/f)
el grupoband / group
el conciertoconcert
el instrumentoinstrument
tocar la guitarrato play the guitar
tocar el pianoto play the piano
escuchar músicato listen to music
el poppop (music)
el rockrock (music)
el raprap
la música clásicaclassical music
relajanterelaxing
animado/alively, upbeat
desde hace + timefor (ongoing duration) — (Higher)

Grammar focus 1 — desde hace + present: Spanish uses the present tense (NOT the perfect) to express an action that started in the past and is still happening. English says 'I have been listening…'; Spanish says escucho (present). Structure: verb (present) + desde hace + time expression. Example: Toco la guitarra desde hace tres años. (I have been playing the guitar for three years.) Escucho música pop desde hace dos años. (I have been listening to pop music for two years.)

Grammar focus 2 — comparatives: más + adjective + que (more … than); menos + adjective + que (less … than). Example: El rock es más emocionante que la música clásica. (Rock is more exciting than classical music.) Irregular: bueno → mejor, malo → peor.

Model paragraph: Escucho música todos los días. Me encanta el pop porque es animado y alegre. Toco la guitarra desde hace cuatro años. En mi opinión, los conciertos en directo son más emocionantes que escuchar música en casa. (I listen to music every day. I love pop because it is lively and cheerful. I have been playing the guitar for four years. In my opinion, live concerts are more exciting than listening to music at home.)

bronze.question: What does 'Toco la guitarra desde hace tres años' mean?

misconceptions.message: You picked this because 'toco' looks like a simple past action. But 'desde hace tres años' shows an action still happening now, so it means 'I have been playing', not something finished years ago.
You picked this thinking 'desde hace' points to something starting later. Actually it describes an ongoing action from the past continuing now, so it's 'I have been playing', not a future plan.
You picked this assuming the action stopped after three years. 'Desde hace' actually signals the guitar-playing is still going on now, meaning 'I have been playing for three years'.

misconceptions.message: You picked this because it sounds like describing an event you attended. But 'encantan' is present tense showing feeling, so it means 'I love', not 'I watched'.
You picked this by mixing up 'encantan' with something negative like boring. Actually 'encantar' expresses strong liking, so this sentence means the opposite: concerts are loved, not boring.
You picked this thinking 'encantan' shows dislike. In fact 'me encantan' means 'I love them', so the sentence expresses enthusiasm for live concerts, not rejection.

method_card.title: Social Media and Online Life
method_card.content:
This lesson covers social media vocabulary, the advantages and disadvantages of being online, and two key grammar structures: relative pronouns que/quien and modal verbs poder/deber.

SpanishEnglish
las redes socialessocial media
el móvil / el smartphonemobile phone / smartphone
compartirto share
publicarto post / publish
seguir a alguiento follow someone
el seguidor / la seguidorafollower (m/f)
el tiempo de pantallascreen time
puede ser adictivoit can be addictive
mantenerse en contactoto stay in touch
el ciberacosocyberbullying (Higher)
aunquealthough
por un lado… por otro ladoon one hand… on the other hand
debería(mos)I/we should
se puede + infinitiveyou can / one can

Grammar focus 1 — relative pronouns: Use que for things and people ('that/which/who'): una aplicación que uso todos los días (an app that I use every day). Use quien/quienes for people after a preposition: la persona con quien hablo (the person I talk to / with whom I talk). Note: que is never replaced by quien when it is the direct object connector — use que for 'the person that I see' (la persona que veo).

Grammar focus 2 — modal verbs: poder (can/be able to) + infinitive and deber (should/must) + infinitive. In Spanish, the subject pronoun is normally omitted: debes reducir (you should reduce), podemos compartir (we can share). Conditional debería(mos) is softer: deberíamos limitar (we should limit).

Model paragraph: Uso las redes sociales todos los días. Aunque son útiles para mantenerse en contacto con amigos, pueden ser adictivas. Creo que deberíamos limitar nuestro tiempo de pantalla para que no afecte nuestros estudios. (I use social media every day. Although they are useful for staying in touch with friends, they can be addictive. I think we should limit our screen time so that it does not affect our studies.)

method_card.title: Gaming and Digital Entertainment
method_card.content:
This lesson covers video games, online gaming and digital habits. Key grammar: desde hace + present for ongoing duration, time markers, and comparatives.

SpanishEnglish
el videojuegovideo game
la consolagames console
jugar en líneato play online
el juego en líneaonline game
el ordenadorcomputer
la tabletatablet
los juegos de aventuraadventure games
los juegos de estrategiastrategy games
los juegos de deportessports games
jugar con amigos en líneato play with friends online
pasar tiempoto spend time
al día / a la semanaper day / per week
desde hace + timefor (ongoing duration)
el control parentalparental controls
la adicción / la dependenciaaddiction / dependence (Higher)

Grammar focus — desde hace + present: To say how long you have been doing something (and you are still doing it), use: verb (present tense) + desde hace + time expression. Example: Juego a videojuegos desde hace tres años. (I have been playing video games for three years.) Do NOT use the perfect tense here — that is an English habit that Spanish does not share.

Time markers: todos los días (every day), a veces (sometimes), de vez en cuando (from time to time), durante + time (for — duration of a completed period), desde hace + time (for — ongoing to now).

Model paragraph: Juego a videojuegos desde hace dos años. Prefiero los juegos de aventura porque son más emocionantes que los juegos de deportes. Suelo jugar en línea con mis amigos los fines de semana durante dos horas. (I have been playing video games for two years. I prefer adventure games because they are more exciting than sports games. I usually play online with my friends at weekends for two hours.)

exam_context.frequency: Core topic — gaming and digital life appear across all papers in Theme 4

Respond in JSON: {"quality":"excellent|good|needs_work|not_valid","feedback":"2-3 sentences about grammar accuracy","improvement":"optional specific correction"}

wrong.Gusto: Gusto is not how this works. Use me gusta (with indirect object pronoun) or simply prefiero (I prefer).

misconceptions.message: You picked this because 'jugué' looks like a simple past action. But 'desde hace cuatro años' with the present tense shows an action still continuing now, so it means an ongoing four years of playing.
You picked this thinking it describes a past habit that's stopped. Actually 'desde hace' with a present tense verb signals something that started in the past and is still happening now.

silver.question: Put these words in the correct order to form a sentence

steps.label: Step 1
steps.content: Juego = I play (present tense). a videojuegos = video games (note: jugar a — you need a after jugar).

steps.label: Step 2
steps.content: desde hace dos años = for two years (ongoing, up to now). Spanish uses the present tense here; English uses 'I have been playing'.

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: I have been playing video games for two years.

worked_examples.question: Translate to English: Juego a videojuegos desde hace dos años.

steps.label: Step 1
steps.content: He jugado is the perfect tense (I have played). In Spanish, desde hace is always used with the present tense, not the perfect.

steps.label: Step 2
steps.content: The perfect tense implies a completed action. Desde hace expresses an ongoing action (still happening now), so the present is correct.

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: The correct sentence is: Juego a videojuegos desde hace tres años.

worked_examples.question: Spot the difference: why is 'He jugado a videojuegos desde hace tres años' incorrect?
